title: Identity from the caller, credentials on the server
subtitle: An agent is who it authenticated as, never who it says it is, and it never holds a key it does not need
lede: The confused-deputy problem is the standing failure of agent systems: an agent acting for one principal is talked into acting for another, or holds a credential that leaks into a transcript. I remove it by construction. Identity is derived from how a caller authenticated, never from an argument in a tool call. Credentials for external services live on the server side of a gateway, are minted per identity where the platform allows it, and are never handed to a model. A gateway between agents and the outside world authenticates the agent, derives its assignment or employee identity from that authentication, and performs the external call itself with credentials it holds.
quote: Anything that works by trusting what an agent says about itself is a design that has not failed yet.
evidence: Identity and least privilege for AI agents: identity derived on the server from how an agent authenticated, never from an argument in a tool call.

Credential brokering and secrets management: external credentials held behind a gateway and minted per identity on the server, never handed to a model, with the repository credential held by a gatekeeper agent.
Digital-employee identity: every meeting action names the digital employee it acts for, with employee tokens minted on the server.
author: Corey James
